question: Does God work on the Sabbath?
summary: Genesis 2:2-3 has God resting on the seventh day after finishing creation and sanctifying that day as a day of rest. John 5:16-17 has Jesus explicitly declaring that 'my Father is working until now, and I also am working,' to defend Sabbath healing.

reconcile.connective: The commentators uniformly distinguish two senses of "work": God ceased only from creating, never from upholding and governing, so Genesis 2 and John 5:17 both stand.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, who catalogued the pair in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, presses that Genesis has God resting on the seventh day while John 5:17 has him working without pause — so God both does and does not keep the Sabbath.

pd_work.note: Clarke treats this exact passage-pair head-on, distinguishing God's rest from creating from his unceasing providential 'continual energy' — the public-domain anchor for the harmonization, surfaced on this row and keyed to John 5:17.

link.title: GotQuestions: What did God do on the seventh day of creation?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment that explicitly cites John 5:17 to argue God ceased only from new creative work, not from sustaining activity — directly on this contradiction.

excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: God created the world in six days: on the seventh he rested from all creating acts, and set it apart to be an everlasting memorial of his work. But, though he rested from creating, he never ceased from preserving and governing that which he had formed: in this respect he can keep no sabbaths; for nothing can continue to exist, or answer the end proposed by the Divine wisdom and goodness, without the continual energy of God.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the row's tension: God rested from CREATING (Genesis 2) but never ceased PRESERVING/GOVERNING (John 5:17), so the two senses of 'work' are different and both passages hold. The cleanest single-voice statement of the harmonization.
excerpts.source_note_text: My Father worked hitherto, and I work - Or, As my Father worketh until now, etc., καθως being understood. God created the world in six days: on the seventh he rested from all creating acts, and set it apart to be an everlasting memorial of his work. But, though he rested from creating, he never ceased from preserving and governing that which he had formed: in this respect he can keep no sabbaths; for nothing can continue to exist, or answer the end proposed by the Divine wisdom and goodness, without the continual energy of God. So I work - I am constantly employed in the same way, governing and supporting all things, comforting the wretched, and saving the lost; and to me, in this respect, there is no sabbath.
